quick_skim.title: EMPIRIC: Experiment-Driven Learning of Residual World Models for Robot Planning
quick_skim.abstract: A robot should be able to learn through experiments how unfamiliar objects behave and interact, then plan with that knowledge. It need not start from scratch: physics engines supply knowledge of motion and contact, but can omit entire mechanisms, such as glue curing, water heating, or wind. We present EMPIRIC, an agent that learns a residual world model: a physics engine extended with code for the missing mechanisms. The learned programs can introduce new forces, constraints, and hidden state, and Bayesian inference estimates their parameters and states from noisy observations. The resulting model lets the agent predict the outcomes of actions, choose informative experiments, and revise its hypotheses when predictions fail. Across five simulated domains, EMPIRIC learns interpretable, reusable models, and solves more tasks with fewer environment interactions than all three baselines. On a physical robot, it learns wind forces and domino masses to solve a manipulation task. Website and code: https://yichao-liang.github.io/empiric

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: EMPIRIC learns a residual world model by extending a physics engine with programs for missing mechanisms, using Bayesian inference to estimate parameters so a robot can predict, experiment, and revise hypotheses.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 机器人应能通过实验学习陌生对象的行为并据此规划，但物理引擎虽提供运动与接触知识，却会遗漏胶固化、水加热或风等机制。本文提出EMPIRIC，在物理引擎上学习残差世界模型，用程序引入新的力、约束与隐藏状态，并以贝叶斯推断从含噪观测中估计参数与状态。该模型使智能体能够预测动作结果、选择信息量大的实验并在预测失败时修正假设，在五个仿真环境中验证，为机器人自主学习世界模型并规划提供了新范式。
